correctness.rationale: Divide the scalar resolvent sum F_m(λ) by √λ; each term becomes (4/π)sech((8ℓ−log λ)/2). The infinite lattice sum is periodic in log λ with period 8. The angular Fourier transform of sech(u/2)/(2π) is sech(πω), by the beta integral with substitution t=e^u, so its periodization has exactly the stated Fourier coefficients. The positive and alternating series give R_+>1>R_->0. All phases and finite truncations are bounded above by C*=1+4/(e^(π²/4)−1)<√2. The resolvent equals the positive Neumann series for an inverse of (2m²+t)I−m²(S+Sᵀ); every pair is linked by a walk, so each resolvent has strictly positive entries. This makes the off-diagonal B_m entries negative. B_m annihilates constants, and its diagonal is bounded by F_m(4m²)≤2mC*<4m by spectral positivity and monotonicity of F_m. This proves strict stochasticity. The CFL uses the nodal diagonal 2m², not the maximal eigenvalue 4m²; F_m(2m²)/(4m)≤(√2/4)C*<1/2 agrees with the cited pure-diffusion restriction. The Nyquist eigenvalue is 4m², and the sinc truncation error there is O(m e^(−4m)); rounding the two mesh sequences preserves limiting phases 0 and 4. Thus m_j^+ gives 0.31588529… and m_j^− gives 0.65514027…, versus the target forward-Euler multiplier 1/2. The printed numerical pair follows the order R_−,R_+, not m_j^+,m_j^−; the displayed equations give the correct correspondence. Inspection of checker.py and a separate bounded calculation of the sums and j=1,…,6 support the constants, not the all-mesh proof. The result is not an inconsistency claim for fixed smooth data or for refined quadrature.

evidence: The maximum-principle theorem gives nonnegative convex weights under the CFL, not the sign-changing spectral error. Its main formulation has boundary conditions; §2.2 explicitly notes the analogous periodic treatment.
The quadrature sources estimate exponential error with refined spacing and controlled truncation, not the asymptotic phase variation at nonvanishing spacing.

The frozen result directly proves strict positivity in its periodic example rather than relying on a strict analogue of the published maximum principle.

value.rationale: This supplies a useful numerical benchmark with a clear distinction: a strict maximum principle and mass conservation can coexist with a mesh-persistent high-frequency accuracy defect of either sign. The standard periodic linear-element setting and explicit signed damping constants permit a direct test of a positivity-preserving discretization. It is not a claim against methods that refine their quadrature spacing.
